findings.title: Redirect path passes through an insecure HTTP hop
findings.explanation: Visiting the old domain redirects through three steps before landing on the final site, and one of those steps (http://new-domain.example.com) is unencrypted HTTP. Anyone intercepting traffic on that middle step could see or tamper with the request before it reaches the secure final site.
findings.recommendation: Update the redirect on old-domain.example.com to point directly to the final HTTPS URL (https://new-domain.example.com/home), removing the intermediate HTTP hop.

findings.title: Old domain redirects through multiple hops to reach new site
findings.explanation: Requests to old-domain.example.com go through 3 redirects before reaching the final page. Each redirect adds extra round-trip time for visitors and search engines, slowing down page loads and diluting SEO value from links pointing at the old domain.
findings.recommendation: Set up a single direct redirect from the old domain straight to the final destination URL instead of chaining through multiple intermediate addresses.

findings.title: No SPF record configured for domain
findings.explanation: The domain has no SPF (Sender Policy Framework) TXT record. Without it, there's no rule telling email providers which servers are allowed to send mail on behalf of this domain, making it easier for attackers to spoof emails that appear to come from this domain.
findings.recommendation: Add an SPF TXT record to the domain's DNS settings specifying which mail servers are authorized to send email for this domain.

findings.title: No DMARC record configured for domain
findings.explanation: There is no DMARC record for this domain. DMARC tells receiving mail servers what to do with messages that fail authentication checks, helping prevent phishing emails that impersonate this domain.
findings.recommendation: Publish a DMARC TXT record (starting with a monitoring policy such as p=none) at _dmarc.old-domain.example.com and adjust the policy over time.

findings.title: TLS certificate is valid and not near expiry
findings.explanation: The site's TLS certificate is issued by Let's Encrypt, uses modern TLSv1.3, and has 60 days remaining before expiration. This is a healthy signal and not an immediate concern.
findings.recommendation: No action needed now; ensure the certificate auto-renewal process is in place before it approaches expiration.
